questions.key_step: Put $3-x^2=t^2$ so that $x\,dx=-t\,dt$ and $x^2=3-t^2$ turns the integrand into a polynomial in $t$.
questions.justification: One substitution with a polynomial result and a constant fixed by the given value; below the level-3 integration anchors.

questions.key_step: Recognise the bracket as $f(x)+f'(x)$ with $f(x)=\frac{x\sin^{-1}x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}$, so the integral is $e^xf(x)$.
questions.justification: Indefinite integration of JEE Main standard: routine chain of standard moves.

questions.key_step: The exponents add to $2$, so factor out $(x+15)^2$ and substitute $t=\frac{x-11}{x+15}$, whose differential is $\frac{26\,dx}{(x+15)^2}$.
questions.justification: Indefinite integration of JEE Main standard: routine chain of standard moves.

questions.key_step: Repeated integration by parts (tabular method) for polynomial $\times$ trigonometric, and $g'(x)=x^3\sin x$ directly.

questions.key_step: Put $x^{1/4}=t$: then $dx=4t^3dt$ and the integrand becomes the rational function $\frac{4t^2}{1+t}$.

questions.key_step: Divide by $\cos^2x$ and put $\tan x=t$ to compare with $\frac1{12}\tan^{-1}(3t)$; the maximum of $a\sin x+b\cos x$ is $\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$.
questions.justification: Indefinite integration of JEE Main standard: routine chain of standard moves.

questions.key_step: Write $\sin^2x(1-\cot x)^2=(\sin x-\cos x)^2$, divide by $\cos^2x$ and put $\tan x=t$ to get $\int\frac{6\,dt}{(t-1)^2}$.
questions.justification: Indefinite integration of JEE Main standard: routine chain of standard moves.

questions.key_step: Convert to $\frac{2\cos x-\sin x}{3\cos x+\sin x}$ and write the numerator as $a\,(\text{denominator})'+b\,(\text{denominator})$.
questions.justification: Indefinite integration of JEE Main standard: routine chain of standard moves.

questions.key_step: Put $t=\tan^{-1}\left(x^3+x^{-3}\right)$; then $dt$ reproduces $\frac{3(x^8-x^2)}{x^{12}+3x^6+1}dx$ and the integral is $\frac13\int\frac{dt}t$.
questions.justification: Indefinite integration of JEE Main standard: routine chain of standard moves.

questions.key_step: After simplifying to $\frac{(1+\sin^2x)\cos x}{1+\sin^4x}$, put $\sin x=t$ and divide by $t^2$: $\int\frac{1+t^{-2}}{t^2+t^{-2}}dt$ with $u=t-\frac1t$.
questions.justification: Indefinite integration of JEE Main standard: a hidden substitution or two-stage chain; closest to a level-3 integration anchor.

questions.key_step: Split the numerator; each part becomes $\frac{\sec^2x\,dx}{\sqrt{\tan x\cos\theta-\sin\theta}}$ or the cosecant analogue, because $\sec x\sin(x-\theta)=\cos\theta\tan x-\sin\theta$.
questions.justification: Indefinite integration of JEE Main standard: a hidden substitution or two-stage chain; closest to a level-3 integration anchor.

questions.key_step: $x\sec^2x+\tan x=(x\tan x+1)'$, so integrate $x^2\cdot\frac{w'}{w^2}$ by parts with $w=x\tan x+1$.
questions.justification: Indefinite integration of JEE Main standard: a hidden substitution or two-stage chain; closest to a level-3 integration anchor.

questions.key_step: With $f=\sin^2x$ and $g=\cos x$: $f'g+g'=\cos x\sin2x-\sin x$, so the integrand is $\frac{d}{dx}\left(e^{f}g\right)$.

questions.key_step: With $t=\left(\frac xe\right)^{2x}$, $\ln t=2x(\ln x-1)$ and $\frac{dt}{t}=2\ln x\,dx$, which supplies the $\log_ex\,dx$.

questions.key_step: Since $(\sqrt{1+x^2}+x)(\sqrt{1+x^2}-x)=1$, the integrand is $\left(\sqrt{1+x^2}+x\right)^{19}$; put $z=\sqrt{1+x^2}+x$ after $x=\tan\theta$.

questions.key_step: Pull one factor $x^{-1}$ out of the root so the integrand is $\left(x^{-2}+x^{-4}\right)\left(3x^{-1}+x^{-3}\right)^{1/23}$, and put $t=3x^{-1}+x^{-3}$.

questions.key_step: Differentiate both sides: the derivative of the right side over the common denominator $2\sqrt{x^2+x+1}$ must have numerator $2(2x^2+5x+9)$.
